system.name: HNLPU
system.one_liner: a chip architecture that physically hardwires LLM weight parameters into the computational fabric via metal interconnects instead of silicon multiplier cells, for extreme energy efficiency in LLM inference

content.subject: how metal-embedding replaces cell-embedding's one-multiplier-per-input datapath with shared per-weight-value accumulators and multipliers

panels.label: ❶ Cell-embedding
panels.differs: baseline: one dedicated 4b multiplier per input (16 shown, 2,880 in the real design), weights stored in silicon device cells

panels.label: ❷ Metal-embedding
panels.differs: bit-serial (1b) inputs are routed by weight value to only 4 shared accumulators (POPCNT) that count inputs sharing the same weight; each count is multiplied once by its unique weight, the 4 per-weight products are summed, then deserialized before activation; weights are embedded as metal wiring instead of silicon cells

content.key_idea: Metal-embedding replaces cell-embedding's one dedicated multiplier per input with metal wiring that routes inputs sharing a weight value into a shared POPCNT accumulator, multiplying by each unique weight only once instead of once per input.
content.reading_order: Top panel: left to right across 16 inputs into the multiplier row, down through the adder tree to sigma; bottom panel repeats this with routing and shared accumulators.

summary: Figure 4 contrasts the two multiplier architectures behind the paper's Hardwired-Neuron (HN) design. Panel 1 (Cell-Embedding, the conventional baseline) shows 16 example inputs, each 4 bits wide, each driving its own dedicated constant-weight multiplier (colour-coded by one of 4 example unique weight values a-d); all 16 products feed a large adder tree and then an activation (sigma) unit. Panel 2 (Metal-Embedding, the paper's approach) instead serializes each input to 1 bit and routes it, via hardwired metal connections rather than silicon multiplier cells, to a shared POPCNT-style accumulator for its weight value; only 4 multipliers are needed (one per unique weight) instead of 16, and their products are summed, deserialized, and activated. The figure visually argues that grouping inputs by shared weight value before multiplying, instead of after, is what lets Hardwired-Neurons collapse a huge per-input multiplier array down to one multiplier per unique weight value.
summary_zh: 图4对比两种硬件神经元乘法：①基线Cell-Embedding中16个输入各驱专属乘法器，求和后经sigma激活；②Metal-Embedding将输入按位串行化，路由到共享POPCNT累加器，每个权重仅需一个乘法器，再求和解串激活。
